liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer calls the transition one of the best ever and the whole show jaw-droppingly good [25]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-03-22.mtx.seamons.113144.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 161 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd1990-03-22.165885.mtx.seamons.ht090.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 157 min [6]
- **gd1990-03-22.152792.3-Source-MTX.photoLeon.t-flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 163 min [7]
- **gd90-03-22.sbd-matrix.aj.453.sbefail.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 151 min; rated 4.32/5 by 25 [16]
- **gd90-03-22.sbd.bertha-ashley.21433.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 151 min; rated 4.34/5 by 50 [22]. Said about its sound: Recording lacks high and low end richness but feels like being in the auditorium; Sound quality is excellent, close to SBD but not quite, with deep echo; Not pure SBD but features deep echo and a nice smooth flow to the music [31][32][33]

## Around the show

- Brent was magical and Jerry was on fire during the performance [26]
- Brent sang the whole Hey Jude, forgetting words in spots, appearing humble and fun [28]
- Reviewer felt at home when Feel Like a Stranger started, noting Canada's lack of smoke [28]
- Highlights include West L.A., Scarlet>Fire, Sam and Dee, Believe It Or Not, and Truckin [34]
- Squeaky and reviewer snuck onto the floor for the second set [7]
- Makes listener miss the Brent era and remember the Dead's greatness prior to Jerry's haze [29]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-03-22.mtx.seamons.113144.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: flac16: Matrix by Jubal Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (SHN & FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT) [1]. Also: Final performance of Believe It Or Not (10-21-1988) and Hey Jude (03-01-1969) [1]
- **gd1990-03-22.165885.mtx.seamons.ht090.flac16**: source: Matrix by Jubal Hunter Seamons using Soundtrack Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Soundtrack > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) October 2, 2023 [6]. Also: Uses Cutler truck mix and improved audience transfer; SBD had extra ambience but distant crowd [6]
- **gd1990-03-22.152792.3-Source-MTX.photoLeon.t-flac16**: source: Matrix created in Adobe Audition by Joe Noel May 16, 2021 [7]. Also: Thanks to Ray, Ted, John Cutler, David Gans, Charlie Miller, and Jack Schlottman [7]
- **gd90-03-22.sbd-matrix.aj.453.sbefail.shnf**: source: SBD (Matrix)> DAT> CD> EAC> [retracking of d2 w/ SF, no other alteration]> SHN [16]. Also: Files in this profile are from the prior night, 3-21-90, not 3-22-90 [24]
- **gd90-03-22.sbd.bertha-ashley.21433.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [22]. Also: Reviewer questions pedigree, noting the open sound typical of a pre-FM recording; Matrix soundboard made from the 32-track multitrack source [31][35]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1990-03-22 Thu Copps Coliseum, Hamilton, Canada](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1251188640243/grateful-dead-1990-03-22-thu-copps) [37]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1990-03-21 Copps Coliseum, Hamilton, Ontario, Canada - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1990-03-21-copps-coliseum-hamilton-ontario-canada/) [38]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Copps Coliseum - March 22, 1990](https://www.dead.net/show/march-22-1990) [39]
- Poster by Dave Goodwich: [30th Anniversary of The Grateful Dead's Spring '90 Tour: Copps Coliseum, Hamilton, Ontario 3/22/90 - Glide Magazine](https://glidemagazine.com/241736/30th-anniversary-of-the-grateful-deads-spring-90-tour-copps-coliseum-hamilton-ontario-3-22-90/) [40]

claims.text: Files in this profile are from the prior night, 3-21-90, not 3-22-90
Reviewer calls the transition one of the best ever and the whole show jaw-droppingly good
Brent was magical and Jerry was on fire during the performance
Brent sang the whole Hey Jude, forgetting words in spots, appearing humble and fun
Reviewer felt at home when Feel Like a Stranger started, noting Canada's lack of smoke
Makes listener miss the Brent era and remember the Dead's greatness prior to Jerry's haze
Recording lacks high and low end richness but feels like being in the auditorium
Reviewer questions pedigree, noting the open sound typical of a pre-FM recording
Sound quality is excellent, close to SBD but not quite, with deep echo
Not pure SBD but features deep echo and a nice smooth flow to the music
Highlights include West L.A., Scarlet>Fire, Sam and Dee, Believe It Or Not, and Truckin
Matrix soundboard made from the 32-track multitrack source
Final performance of Believe It Or Not (10-21-1988) and Hey Jude (03-01-1969)
Uses Cutler truck mix and improved audience transfer; SBD had extra ambience but distant crowd
Thanks to Ray, Ted, John Cutler, David Gans, Charlie Miller, and Jack Schlottman
Squeaky and reviewer snuck onto the floor for the second set
